html:
SMTO-CFG-0103 — The SMTO website can't start with its current settings

GUID: 3d9dee75-2821-5fce-9d83-360a621aacbf
Slug: public-site-configuration-invalid
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: public

What happened

  • The public SMTO website, which is separate from the SMTO app, has a setting it can't accept, such as an address that isn't a public https address. It didn't start, so visitors can't reach it yet.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Read the message in the website's window or log. Most messages name the setting, such as SMTO_SITE_BASE_URL or SMTO_SITE_PORT. Each message points to the one setting that failed.
  2. For a live website, set the address to a public https address with no path, port or login, for example https://example.com, and leave reload and analytics off. The website refuses private, local or insecure addresses and options that aren't finished.
  3. If you set SMTO_SITE_SECURITY_CONTACT, also set SMTO_SITE_SECURITY_EXPIRES to a future date with a time zone, such as 2027-06-30T00:00:00+00:00. A security contact must say until when it's valid.
  4. From the SMTO folder, run python scripts/validate-smto-site-content.py, then start the website again. The check finds remaining problems before visitors see them.

What success looks like

  • The check finishes without an error, and the website opens at its public address.

If it still fails

  • Copy the message and your SMTO_SITE settings, leaving out any passwords, and send them to the person who runs the website. Don't delete the website's data folder or visitor records to get past this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • SiteConfig validation rejected an SMTO_SITE_* setting (environment, port, base or canonical origin, public URL, reload in production, log level, release channel, analytics, or security contact and expiry), so the public website did not start.

What this means

  • Public-site configuration violates deployment environment, port/base/public URL, host/trust, logging/channel, unsupported analytics or security-contact constraints. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • Public-site configuration violates deployment environment, port/base/public URL, host/trust, logging/channel, unsupported analytics or security-contact constraints.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the specific SMTO_SITE field and environment-specific rules; production trust/HTTPS requirements differ from local development.

How to fix it

  • Fix the named SMTO_SITE_* variable: SMTO_SITE_ENV development, production or test; integer SMTO_SITE_PORT 1–65535; an origin-only SMTO_SITE_BASE_URL or SMTO_SITE_CANONICAL_ORIGIN (public HTTPS with no credentials, port or fragment in production); reload off in production; SMTO_SITE_ANALYTICS_ENABLED=0; and a valid mailto or HTTPS security contact with a future, timezone-aware SMTO_SITE_SECURITY_EXPIRES. Run python scripts/validate-smto-site-content.py before restarting.
  • Correct the named SMTO_SITE setting and run the site validation command before restarting the public site.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • Site configuration and the supported validation command pass for the intended deployment environment.
